title: Clubhouse Comms

briefings.headline: Hunt Cameron’s fastballs; don’t chase the curve
briefings.message: Noah Cameron is the high-confidence starter prediction. Look to attack fastballs, especially early, and stay disciplined against his curveball, his strongest pitch by xwOBA allowed. Taylor Ward, Coby Mayo, and Tyler O’Neill have fastball-group advantages. Jackson Holliday also shows a fastball edge, but his pitch-group samples and LHP sample are small. Be ready for Lucas Erceg late; he leads their listed available relievers with 12 saves.
reminders: Ward: fastball-group advantage; offspeed sample is small.
Mayo: hunt fastballs; breaking-ball sample is small.
Holliday: fastball edge, but samples are small.
Stay patient against Cameron’s curveball and changeup.

briefings.headline: Bradish sets the tone: down, changing speeds, and no easy fastballs
briefings.message: Kyle Bradish is rested and ready. Keep the ball down and change speeds, especially to left-handed hitters. Use breaking balls against Bobby Witt Jr., Lane Thomas, and Salvador Perez; avoid predictable fastballs to Witt and Thomas. Against Jac Caglianone, vary locations and keep breaking balls below the zone rather than treating one pitch as a sure weakness. In a close game, prioritize rested setup arms and reserve Anthony Nunez for the finish. Rico Garcia and Andrew Kittredge are limited after pitching yesterday.
reminders: Plan for about five innings with a 90-pitch limit.
Use breaking balls carefully against Caglianone; vary location.
Close late: Yennier Cano and Tyler Wells before Nunez.
Use Garcia and Kittredge only if needed.
